description: Rung-6 clinical differential diagnosis — the clinical/MLE bridge. Each item is a board-style differential: three competing diagnoses with equal priors, three findings, and a likelihood ratio for every (finding, diagnosis) pair. The gold ADJ program declares the priors, a contributes-<LR>-from-<finding>-to-<diagnosis> for each pair, and observes every finding; the ENGINE multiplies the priors by all the likelihood ratios (Bayesian combination) and reports the leading diagnosis, read by the existing decision_leader extractor (no harness or engine change). The reasoning step beyond rung-3 single-finding decisions: the answer is the diagnosis that wins on the COMBINED evidence, while a deliberately planted distractor wins on a single FLASHY finding alone (one huge likelihood ratio, ~1 on the rest). A reasoner that anchors on the salient finding takes the distractor; only carrying every likelihood ratio through the product lands the gold (anchoring bias is the classic board trap). The stem is generated from the data so every prior and likelihood ratio in the program appears verbatim in the stem (no-result-literals gate holds); the five options are distinct diagnosis labels. Twenty real differentials across cardiology, pulmonology, GI, neurology, endocrine, ID, renal, MSK, and pediatrics. Engine selects the combined-evidence leader 20/20 in cached mode, zero wrong. BATCH 2 (r6-21..r6-40): twenty FOUR-way differentials (four scored diagnoses A-D, E=unknown) that add a new reasoning step — a likelihood ratio BELOW 1 ARGUES AGAINST a diagnosis (it multiplies that diagnosis's running product down). So a flashy diagnosis with one strong positive finding can be demoted below a quieter rival once a strong negative (LR<1) finding is carried through. The engine still does prior × ∏ likelihood ratios over the observed findings; only the data and stem change. Batch 2 spans wide-complex tachycardia, RUQ pain, acute vision loss, hypercalcemia, meningoencephalitis, AKI, microcytic anemia, pleural effusion, monoarthritis, pediatric stridor, GI bleed, blistering dermatoses, adrenal disorders, dementia, post-MI chest pain, infectious diarrhea, thrombocytopenia, solitary lung nodule, pelvic pain, and toxic ingestions. Engine selects the combined-evidence leader 40/40 in cached mode, zero wrong.
